title: Data warehouse: BigQuery, Snowflake and Redshift

videos.script: Everything in the last two lessons can be rented: columns, compression, partitions, many machines, storage kept apart from compute. {{rented}} Three products dominate the rented kind: BigQuery from Google, Snowflake, and Redshift from Amazon. {{three}} They agree on almost everything that matters to a model. They all store by column. They all keep data apart from compute. They all run the star schema Ana built, nearly as written. {{agree}} Where they differ is what you pay for. BigQuery can charge for the bytes a query reads. Snowflake charges for the seconds a cluster runs. Redshift charges for the nodes you keep, or the capacity you use. {{pay}} And each one asks you a different question about the physical design. Partition and cluster. Clustering keys on micro-partitions. Distribution keys and sort keys. {{design}} None of the three runs in this lab. So this lesson does what an architect does before signing a contract. It reads the price pages, does the arithmetic on Ana's real data, and writes the same tables in three dialects. {{honest}}
